Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May implementing Law 10/2010; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership; Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the Spanish Companies Act; Law 50/2002 of 26 December on Foundations; Law 49/2002 of 23 December on the tax regime for non-profit entities and tax incentives for patronage.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish S.L. must have a registered office in Spain and the address must correspond to the location of its effective management or principal establishment under the Companies Act. A commercial virtual office may be used for registered-office and correspondence purposes if the provider permits legal domicile use, maintains reliable access to statutory notices, and supports identification and inspection requirements. It is unsuitable as the sole substance for a grant-making or charitable operation involving cross-border funds, regulated payment activity, employees, material assets, donor due diligence, or beneficiary administration. The submitted structure is legally inconsistent if intended to operate as a private charitable foundation: an S.L. is a commercial limited-liability company, whereas a Spanish foundation requires a public-benefit purpose, endowment, founding deed, Protectorate oversight, and registration under Law 50/2002.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for deed registration; Public Notary for deed execution.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Arts. 19-22, 23, 102, 210-213; Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); supplementary foundation rules under Ley 50/2002 de Fundaciones if a registered foundation is authorized.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de constitución and subsequent inscription in the Registro Mercantil (public incorporation deed and commercial registry filing).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 30 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Minimum share capital for an SL is €3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at formation. Payment must be evidenced by a bank certificate delivered to the notary; no escrow account is required by law.

Funding & unlock path: Office premises must obtain a municipal occupancy or opening certificate (declaración responsable or licencia de apertura), fire safety certification, and a certificate of compliance with workplace safety under Ley 31/1995 and Real Decreto 486/1997 (workplace health and safety).

Paid-in capital rule: Minimum share capital for an SL is €3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at formation. Payment must be evidenced by a bank certificate delivered to the notary; no escrow account is required by law.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The undersigned founding members, having decided to incorporate a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under Spanish law, hereby resolve unanimously: (i) to subscribe and pay in full the company’s share capital, not less than €3,000, and accept the corresponding participaciones; (ii) to approve the draft articles of association and establish the registered office at the address stated in the deed; (iii) to appoint the initial administrators named in the deed; and (iv) to execute the public deed of incorporation and take all steps before the Commercial Registry and tax authorities. The officers are authorized to sign forms and open bank accounts.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Ministerio de Justicia – Registro de Fundaciones / Protectorado de Fundaciones; additionally the competent municipal Ayuntamiento for urban activity and opening licenses.

Category: Inscripción en el Registro de Fundaciones / Autorización del Protectorado (if foundation status is granted); Licencia de apertura y actividad from the municipal authority for physical premises.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

For a resident Spanish SL: (1) incorporate before a Notary and submit Modelo 030 to obtain a provisional NIF; (2) after inscription in the Mercantile Registry, file the definitive NIF application with AEAT within two months attaching the deed, registry certificate, and representative's ID; (3) file Modelo 036/037 to enrol in the Census of Entrepreneurs, and simultaneously register for Impuesto sobre Sociedades, IVA, and withholding obligations. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Spanish permanent establishment: appoint a tax representative, obtain a non-resident NIF via Modelo 030, and if taxable activities are carried out, register for VAT via Modelo 036/037; apostilled and legalized incorporation documents and power of attorney are required.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — For a resident Spanish SL: (1) incorporate before a Notary and submit Modelo 030 to obtain a provisional NIF; (2) after inscription in the Mercantile Registry, file the definitive NIF application with AEAT within two months attaching the deed, registry certificate, and representative's ID; (3) file Modelo 036/037 to enrol in the Census of Entrepreneurs, and simultaneously register for Impuesto sobre Sociedades, IVA, and withholding obligations. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Spanish permanent establishment: appoint a tax representative, obtain a non-resident NIF via Modelo 030, and if taxable activities are carried out, register for VAT via Modelo 036/037; apostilled and legalized incorporation documents and power of attorney are required.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; an SL is mandatorily taxed as a separate legal entity under the Ley 27/2014 Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Main optional statutory elections include: (i) group fiscal consolidation election under Art. 67 LIS (70%/75% shareholding requirements and simultaneous filing conditions); (ii) the transitional ETVE special regime for holding companies with foreign securities; (iii) the AIE/UTE partially transparent regime (only where the SL itself participates as a member, not as the entity being classified). Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD are automatically applicable, with no elective carve-out.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general turnover threshold triggering VAT registration: any person/entity making taxable supplies of goods or services in Spanish territory must register via Modelo 036/037 before commencing activities. The €250,000 and €100,000 thresholds are used only for the simplified SME VAT regime eligibility, not as a registration exemption.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods to non-EU destinations are exempt with credit (effective 0%) under Art. 21 LIVA where the goods are definitively dispatched or transported to a non-EU territory, Ceuta, Melilla, or the Canary Islands, and the exporter possesses a valid NIF-IVA and evidence of exit from the EU within 90 days. Services directly relating to exported goods (e.g., international transport, loading, stevedoring, inspections, forwarding and intermediary services), certain processing services on movable goods intended for export, and services whose place of supply is outside Spain under B2B rules are outside the scope of Spanish VAT with a corresponding right to deduct input VAT attributable to those operations.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA) with customs exit validation records
  • Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing physical export
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency consideration

No centralized real-time invoice clearance or single digital stamping by AEAT applies to all taxpayers. Large companies with turnover above €6,000,000 and entities under special regimes (including VAT groups and export/import operators) must submit invoice records to AEAT in near real-time under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) via secure API/web services. Under the Veri*factu system (Royal Decree 1007/2023), billing software must generate invoices with a QR-linked digital signature and integrity mechanism, with phased mandatory compliance through 2025/2026.

The exporter must retain export declarations, transport documents, invoices, payment proof, and forex records for at least four years (the VAT statute of limitations). AEAT may retroactively deny zero-rating, assess the VAT together with late-payment interest and a surcharge; penalties range from 50% to 150% of the understated VAT (Art. 191 LGT). Where fraudulent intent is established and the amount defrauded exceeds €120,000, criminal liability may arise under Arts. 305-308 Código Penal, including imprisonment, fines, and loss of tax benefits, with full clawback across all open prior periods.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain maintains a fully convertible Euro currency regime with unrestricted capital account movements and liberalized current account transactions. Capital contributions and equity injections face no convertibility restrictions. Profit remittances and grant distributions are freely convertible subject only to standard Spanish withholding tax (19% base rate, treaty-reduced) and Form 720 foreign asset reporting thresholds. No capital controls or profit remittance hurdles apply to legitimate philanthropic endowment operations or EU-based grant flows.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Not applicable. The entity conducts endowment management and philanthropic grant distribution rather than goods export. Spanish exporters must surrender foreign exchange proceeds to authorized banks within ten working days; this obligation does not extend to non-trading financial or charitable entities.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Revolut Fit: High

Low viability for offshore digital EMIs. Spanish SL entities require local banking relationships for corporate accounts and grant distributions. Platforms such as N26 or Revolut may support limited operations but cannot fully satisfy AML, tax reporting, or cross-border grant compliance without integration to a Spanish tier-1 bank.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Anonymous or opaque beneficial ownership structures

Root cause: Anonymous or opaque beneficial ownership structures

Defense evidence: Registro Mercantil extract, director and beneficial owner identification documents, source-of-funds declarations, and grant agreement copies to establish legitimate philanthropic endowment origins.
Unexplained large inbound capital transfers

Root cause: Unexplained large inbound capital transfers

Defense evidence: Philanthropic grant contracts, endowment charter excerpts, tax residency proofs, and matching bank statements to substantiate legitimate grant receipt purposes.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 to Spanish IBAN accounts. Purpose codes must reference 'capital contribution' or 'grant receipt' for philanthropic endowments. All transactions require matching to corporate statements and supporting grant documentation. Large amounts trigger Form 720 reporting.Outbound grant distributions via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA for Euro transfers. Non-Euro settlements use correspondent banking networks. Commercial LCs are not standard for grant payments; wire transfers constitute the primary rail. All disbursements must align with documented philanthropic purposes to mitigate AML risk.Forward contracts for currency risk mitigation on non-Euro exposuresCurrency swaps for multi-currency liquidity managementNon-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for hedging LatAm currency exposures without physical delivery

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Low viability for offshore digital EMIs. Spanish SL entities require local banking relationships for corporate accounts and grant distributions. Platforms such as N26 or Revolut may support limited operations but cannot fully satisfy AML, tax reporting, or cross-border grant compliance without integration to a Spanish tier-1 bank.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% standard Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Certain qualifying newly created entities may apply a 15% rate during the first tax period in which they obtain a positive tax base and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse conditions. Qualifying micro-enterprises may receive transitional reduced rates under the applicable annual Budget Law.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish company to a non-resident. The rate may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in Spain. The domestic participation exemption for qualifying EU parent companies generally requires, among other conditions, a minimum 5% participation or qualifying acquisition value, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment, subject-to-tax conditions and anti-abuse compliance.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200 is due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing period is 1 to 25 July. If the tax period is shorter than 12 months, the deadline is calculated from that period's end. Modelo 202 and Modelo 222 are generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October and December, subject to AEAT electronic-filing rules. If the deadline falls on a non-business day, the applicable electronic filing rule extends it to the next business day.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally filed and paid within the first 20 calendar days of April, October and December. The calculation method may be based on the prior year's final tax liability or the current-period tax base, depending on the taxpayer's statutory status and election.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Identification and tax period Enter the Spanish tax identification number (NIF), legal name, registered address, tax period start and end dates, legal form, and relevant census information. A non-resident shareholder must not be reported as the taxpayer merely because it owns the SL. The Spanish SL files under its own NIF. Non-resident directors, shareholders and related parties must be identified using their foreign tax identification numbers where required. A return with no tax payable may still attract a fixed penalty, commonly EUR 200, normally reduced by 50% where legally available for voluntary compliance without prior requirement. Late or inaccurate Modelo 232, information returns, accounting records or withholding returns may trigger separate fixed or proportional penalties.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File documentation is generally not required for controlled transactions with the same related person or entity where the aggregate arm's-length value for the tax period does not exceed EUR 250,000, subject to statutory exclusions and special documentation rules. Documentation is required for higher-risk or specifically regulated transactions regardless of reliance on general thresholds. Master File requirements generally apply to Spanish entities belonging to groups, with simplified or non-applicable documentation rules for groups whose consolidated net turnover is below EUR 45 million, subject to statutory exceptions. Form 232 reporting may be required where transaction-value thresholds are exceeded, including material transactions with the same related party or specific transaction categories.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime. Substance is nevertheless material under Spanish transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-abuse rule, the anti-tax-avoidance rule, controlled foreign company rules, EU anti-hybrid rules, beneficial-ownership doctrine, treaty principal-purpose tests and permanent-establishment rules. The Spanish company should maintain genuine decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or appropriate infrastructure, documented charitable or investment activities, independent governance, commercial rationale and risk control proportionate to its functions. A paper SL used solely to route dividends, royalties, interest or grants may face denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization, transfer-pricing adjustments, withholding assessments and penalties.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Misclassification of legal form or charitable status

Statutory sanction: Tax reassessment, repayment of unlawfully claimed benefits, late-payment interest, tax-infringement penalties generally ranging from fixed amounts to 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax depending on the infringement, and possible loss of the special regime.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur civil liability for tax damage, accounting breaches and misuse of assets. Criminal liability can arise if conduct satisfies tax-fraud, fraud, insolvency or document-offence thresholds. Imprisonment is not automatic.
Tax evasion and fraudulent tax returns

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties may reach 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, plus tax, interest and collection charges. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax and period may constitute a criminal offence, generally punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded; aggravated cases may carry higher penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors, de facto directors and participating officers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, civil restitution, asset seizure and disqualification from public office or commercial management. Travel restrictions may be ordered only by competent authorities or courts where legally justified.
Shell company and artificial profit diversion

Statutory sanction: Denial of treaty or directive relief, beneficial-ownership challenge, withholding-tax reassessment, transfer-pricing adjustment, general anti-abuse application, interest and penalties. Transactions may be recharacterized according to their actual legal and economic substance.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil liability for abusive transactions and, where intentional fraud is proven, criminal liability. Corporate separateness is not disregarded merely because the company is small or foreign-owned.
Transfer-pricing non-compliance

Statutory sanction: Primary tax adjustments, withholding consequences, compensating adjustments where available, documentation penalties and penalties for inaccurate or incomplete information. Documentation-related penalties may be fixed per missing or incorrect data point or linked to adjusted amounts under Spanish tax rules.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable for intentional concealment, gross governance failures or unlawful distributions. Routine pricing disagreement does not itself create criminal liability.
Improper profit distribution and capital-maintenance breach

Statutory sanction: Recipient repayment, director liability for restitution, corporate-law penalties, possible dissolution or insolvency consequences, and tax treatment of the distribution as a dividend, remuneration, concealed distribution or non-deductible expense.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly liable for repayment and creditor damage and may face disqualification or insolvency liability. Imprisonment requires separate criminal conduct such as fraud or asset concealment.
Withholding-tax failure

Statutory sanction: Assessment of unpaid withholding, late-payment interest, surcharge, penalties generally calculated by reference to the unpaid amount, and possible secondary liability for the payer.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil or administrative liability where they knowingly authorize non-compliant payments or frustrate collection. Criminal liability requires proof of a separate offence.
Anti-money laundering and terrorist-financing breach

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish AML law, breaches may be classified as minor, serious or very serious, with fines that can reach substantial amounts and, for serious or very serious breaches, percentages of the relevant transaction or annual turnover, together with public reprimand, authorization consequences and management sanctions.

Director personal liability: Directors and compliance officers may be personally sanctioned, disqualified or prosecuted for knowing participation, concealment or facilitation. Asset freezes and travel restrictions may arise in sanctions or criminal proceedings where legally ordered.
Sanctions evasion and prohibited beneficiaries

Statutory sanction: Payment blocking, asset freezing, administrative sanctions, confiscation and potential criminal prosecution under applicable Spanish, European Union and international sanctions regimes.

Director personal liability: Directors and authorized signatories may face personal administrative or criminal exposure, asset seizure and court-ordered travel restrictions. Screening, escalation and documented risk-based controls are required.
Accounting, annual-account and corporate-record failure

Statutory sanction: Accounting and Companies Registry penalties, tax reassessment, evidentiary disadvantage, possible closure of the registry sheet, and enhanced penalties where accounting manipulation affects tax liability or creditors.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable for creditor losses, insolvency-related deficiencies, false accounts and obstruction. Criminal exposure may arise for falsification or fraudulent insolvency.
Beneficial-owner and nominee arrangement risk

Statutory sanction: AML enforcement, refusal of bank services, suspicious transaction reporting, freezing or rejection of payments, tax recharacterization and penalties for inaccurate beneficial-owner information.

Director personal liability: Directors may face personal liability for concealment, facilitation or false statements. Corporate limited liability does not protect deliberate criminal conduct.
Unlicensed or unauthorized regulated activity

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines, cessation orders, restitution, invalidation of activities and possible criminal consequences where unauthorized financial activity or fraud is involved.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for unauthorized management, creditor or beneficiary losses and intentional breaches; disqualification and criminal prosecution may follow where statutory thresholds are met.
